question: ______ is used for the separation of components of a mixture containing two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Distillation**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distillation**:
 
• This is a process used to **separate components of a mixture using differences in their boiling points.**
 
• The mixture is heated to a temperature at which** one or more components evaporate, and then the vapor is condensed and collected separately.**
 
• It's commonly used to **purify liquids, such as alcohol or water, or to separate petroleum into various components, from gasoline to tar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbonation:**

 
 
• This is the process of dissolving carbon dioxide in water.
 
• The process usually involves pressure and low temperatures.
 
• When the pressure is reduced, the carbon dioxide is released from the solution as small bubbles,
 
• Which gives the solution a fizzy taste. It is commonly used in the creation of soft drinks.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation:**
 
 
• This is a process in which a substance goes directly from the solid phase to the gas phase, skipping the liquid phase.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) is a common example of a substance that sublimates.
 
• This process can be used to purify certain substances that sublimate, such as iodine or naphthalene (mothballs).
 
 
 
• **Emulsification: **
 
 
• This is the process of mixing two or more immiscible (unblendable) substances.
 
• This is typically accomplished with the help of a third substance called an emulsifier or emulsifying agent
 
• Which is soluble in both of the mixed substances.
 
• Mayonnaise is a common example of an emulsion
 
• Where oil and vinegar (which are normally immiscible) are mixed together using egg yolk as an emulsifier.
